profile.businessSummary: Syrma SGS Technology Limited is an electronics manufacturing services (EMS) company, providing product design, assembly, and manufacturing services for automotive, industrial, and medical sectors.

news.title: Syrma SGS Technology Q2 net profit jumped 83% YoY to ₹117 crore, with revenue rising 73.6% to ₹1,990 crore. EBITDA grew 67.8% to ₹193 crore, driven by automotive and consumer segments, while margins contracted slightly to 9.7%.
Six new stocks including Coromandel, Karur Vysya Bank, and Data Patterns enter the F&O segment today. Joined by CUB, Navin Fluorine, and Syrma SGS, the total count of F&O companies rises to 219.

Syrma SGS reported weak Q2 results as margins dropped 700 basis points due to consumer business headwinds and employee costs. Management plans lower FY27 capex than guided 660 crore rupees and will reassess its consumer business EBITDA breakeven timeline.

Syrma SGS Technology will host an earnings conference call on November 2, 2026, at 10:30 AM IST. The call will discuss unaudited financial results for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026.

JPMorgan rates Dixon Technologies and Amber Enterprises Overweight with targets of Rs 16,200 and Rs 8,350, favoring high ROCE and growth. The brokerage is Underweight on Syrma, Avalon, and Cyient DLM, urging investors to evaluate ROCE alongside earnings growth.

Essencore has partnered with Syrma SGS to strengthen local manufacturing capabilities and expand presence in India. The tie-up is part of Hong Kong-based Essencore's strategy involving initiatives and collaborations with local manufacturers.

Franklin Templeton Mutual Fund sold 110,190 equity shares, representing a 0.1% stake, in Syrma SGS Technology Ltd via an open market transaction on September 30, 2026. Following the sale, Franklin Templeton Mutual Fund's total holding in the company decreased from 5,918,313 shares (3.1%) to 5,808,123 shares (3.1%).

JPMorgan has downgraded Syrma SGS Technology, Avalon Technologies, and Cyient DLM despite 47% EPS growth, arguing that strong earnings growth alone may not justify the premium valuations of the three EMS companies. The brokerage's comparison places revenue growth, earnings growth, return on capital employed (ROCE), and working capital at the centre of the valuation debate.

RBL Bank, Engineers India, Syrma, and JSW Infra rallied up to 7%, hitting 52-week highs before paring gains. Syrma surged 146% YTD, supported by new MedTech facilities, while RBL Bank saw improved asset quality and analyst upgrades.
Syrma SGS Technology plans $600M semiconductor capex, contingent on partner deal.
